proof_checks.precedence: The cleanup phase assigns each duplicated leaf to its least-ranked holder in the chosen minimum cover by deleting all other copies. For a leaf to be kept by a specific view, that view must be ranked earlier than all other original holders of that leaf, making an arrow from the keeper to every other holder necessary. Respecting all such arrows guarantees the keeper is the earliest, making them sufficient. A view can be placed last among the occupied roles if and only if it has no outgoing arrows, meaning it is a sink in the precedence graph. The writer migrates the occupied indices to the first q positions. If the initially blank view B is ranked last, all q positions are already occupied, no migration occurs, and B stays blank. If B is ranked earlier, the first q positions omit the last occupied role, and B receives that donor's entire bundle. When m>q, the subsequent recoloring phase only operates on the first q positions, meaning a last-ranked B cannot be written to during this phase and remains blank.
proof_checks.same_event: In the three-view cases (e.g., rows 184 and 232), B is blank and A is the donor. Exactly three of the six orderings place the reference before A, emitting A's deletion of the duplicated leaf as the first edit. Among these, B receives the surviving donor leaf in two orders and stays blank in the third. In the four-view case with initial state (1,3,13,21), B has only the root, X has leaf 1, R has leaves 2 and 3, and A has leaves 2 and 4. The private leaves force a unique minimum cover of size three, with leaf 2 as the sole duplicate. The source deletes A's leaf 2 first exactly when R precedes A (12 qualifying orders), yielding the exact same post-event state (1,3,13,17). The precedence sinks are A and X. Depending on the rank order, B gains leaf 4 (6 orders), leaf 1 (3 orders), or stays blank (3 orders). This distinguishes the causal contribution of the source deletion from the occurrence of the transfer, as the exact same event and unique cover admit different first acquisitions or silence.
proof_checks.coverage: The audit defines a live event class by requiring B to be the unique blank view immediately before and after A's deletion, as well as throughout the preceding path. This exact both-sides-blank definition ensures B's status is strictly controlled and excludes donor deletions that introduce a second blank view. The replay script exhaustively checks all 74,185 original paths across the eleven domains. It identifies 3,504 classes with the preparation retained. Among these, 1,206 are always silent, 2,040 allow both a write and silence, and 258 always write. Crucially, each of the 258 exceptions lifts to exactly one original ordered starting row, confirming that no class with multiple ordered starts in this comparison forces an acquisition. The formula was checked against all original paths, confirming the predicted outcomes and identifying the 67 classes that admit more than one copying donor.
proof_checks.scope: The structural properties supply the intrinsic roles, the exact source deletion, the full duplicate-cleanup outcome, and the minimum cover. However, the specific first acquisition by the receiver still depends entirely on the caller's unobservable rank order, which determines which sink role acts as the donor or whether B is ranked last and remains silent. Regarding physics, the fixed-order handoff remains an inherited software fact. A physical rule for selecting a transfer and its donor, as well as physical access to the resulting record, remain open questions, leaving the native bridge status open.
